Experts tackle the manosphere, youth misogyny, and toxic algorithms in a live ABC Q&A.
Evidence: Studies, youth surveys, expert panel
#Aletheia #GenderEquality 🌐

ABC News launched an expert Q&A to help parents and teens navigate online misogyny, toxic masculinity influencers, and social media algorithms.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Constructive Engagement

Experts and researchers expose how 23 minutes of scrolling hooks young men on toxic content, leaving 1 in 4 girls feeling unsafe.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.4, +0.3) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Grace. Experts and advocates provide vital empirical clarity on radicalizing algorithms and youth safety.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.2, Uncertainty z: 0)

- ABC Q&A Panel: PASS (+0.8, +0.6) — Evidence-based guidance.

ABC News hosted a live blog featuring developmental pediatricians, psychologists, and advocates addressing the societal impacts of online manosphere content.

The Bright Side:
Transparent public engagement confronts hidden online radicalization head-on.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing a cultural symptom (what teens watch) with the systemic driver (platform recommendation algorithms).

Social Physics Analysis:
Experts deploy a Smart Altruistic loop: transparent data sharing, community coalition, and empathetic support replacing toxic online extraction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When mapping stated intent to ground results, it plots toward systemic empowerment. Transparent dialogue counters manipulative algorithmic loops.

The Unavoidable Truth: Radicalizing algorithms systematically monetize adolescent insecurity.

The Unavoidable Lie: Simple filters alone can fix systemic online misogyny.

Transparent expert analysis exposes how profit-driven recommendation engines weaponize adolescent identity against social cohesion.

It hurts to watch young minds get hijacked by cruelty online, but seeing experts offer real tools gives me hope for healing.

Wild how 20 minutes on TikTok can warp a kid's brain. Glad experts are finally breaking it down.

Topic:Gender Equality

If you're worried about the rise of the manosphere and the messages it's sending teenage boys and men about masculinity, relationships and their place in the world, you're not alone.

It's a complex topic with no easy solution, so we've asked a panel of experts to join us to answer your questions.

We'll be joined by developmental paediatrician Dr Billy Garvey, Dr Zac Seidler from Movember and Genevieve Sheppard from Our Watch.

Follow along live and submit your questions for our experts below.

Key Event

By Georgia Hitch

Given the nature of the manosphere, it's likely that today may touch on some issues that are confronting and difficult.

By Anna Levy

Key Event

By Anna Levy

According to recent research: very.

Research conducted by the Movember Institute of Men's Health found that 68 per cent of young Australian men aged 16-25 engaged with masculinity influencers. That’s more than in the UK (61 per cent) or the US (60 per cent).

A 2024 Dublin City University study found that it took roughly 23 minutes of video watching on either TikTok or YouTube Shorts for the algorithms to start recommending "toxic" content.

Another 2024 study by YouGov and girls' empowerment charity Tomorrow Woman found that 42 per cent of female students said their male peers were influenced by the likes of Andrew Tate and the manosphere.

It also found that one in four female high school students in Australia felt unsafe at school due to these behaviours.

By Anna Levy

We've already got some fantastic questions coming through. Our experts will be clocking on shortly, so please keep them coming.

Key Event

By Georgia Hitch

Earlier this year, the federal government announced it would introduce laws requiring social media companies give users the option to opt in or out of the algorithm on their feeds.

What does this have to do with the manosphere?

Well, advocates like Chanel Contos argue the algorithm exposes young people to misogynistic content and fuels the prevalence of sexual violence and gendered attitudes towards women.

We asked Chanel what regular Australians should know about the campaign and legislation.

"Social media algorithms are increasingly flooding young men's feeds with radical misogynistic content. This is inciting and worsening real-world harm, particularly towards women and girls. The content they're systematically targeted with frequently blames women for any misfortunes they experience, and reinstates harmful and outdated gender stereotypes, like that women shouldn’t hold jobs or earn their own money.

"Fifteen thousand Australians signed our open letter to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and in early September the Government committed to the #FixOurFeeds campaign as part of the Digital Duty of Care legislation — you may have heard it referred to as 'My Feed, My Way'.

"This commitment to allow Australians to turn their algorithms on and off will give people control back over their own data and feeds and disrupt how easily recommendation algorithm systems feed young men and boys manosphere content. The legislation is expected to be introduced into parliament this week, and we're focused on ensuring the detail matches the ambition."

Key Event

By Anna Levy

You might have seen these terms on social media, or heard them from a young man in your life. Here's your (non-exhaustive) manosphere glossary:

These definitions come from UN Women's educational materials on online violence. You can find the full glossary here.

By Georgia Hitch

A new ABC documentary looking into the manosphere, The State of Man, airs tonight, and its host, Marc Fennell, shared how he approached the series.

"No matter who I’m talking to, whether I personally agree with them or not, I like to give people enough space to eventually say the quiet part out loud," he said.

"There’s a version of documentary making where you create big confrontations or stunts because they make great television. Sometimes people just shit stir. And look, I love watching that stuff. But it’s not really what I do.

"I try to approach people with clear eyes and a critical mind, but also genuine curiosity. I’m not sitting there waiting to catch somebody out. I actually want to know why they think what they think.

"The strange thing is that when you give people that space, sometimes you hear some truly cooked things."

You can watch The State of Man tonight at 8pm on ABC TV, or add it to your watchlist and stream it for free on ABC iview.

Key Event

By Georgia Hitch

We're lucky enough to be joined by three experts today to cover a few different areas linked to the manosphere.

Dr Billy Garvey is a developmental paediatrician, researcher and author. He is the founder of Guiding Growing Minds, a social enterprise bringing evidence-based child development science to communities and families across Australia. He's also the co-host of the Pop Culture Parenting podcast.

Genevieve Sheppard  is a former teacher and currently holds the position of principal advisor, respectful relationships education at Our Watch. For over a decade, she has supported governments, education systems and schools to embed evidence-based, whole-of-school approaches to preventing gender-based violence.

Dr Zac Seidler is a clinical psychologist and leading researcher in men's mental health. He is the global director of men's health research at the Movember Institute of Men's Health, leading research focused on how masculinity, culture and social norms influence men's mental health and help-seeking behaviours.

Key Event

By Anna Levy

Hi, and thanks for joining us today.

I'm Anna, and I'll be with you for the next few hours, along with my colleague Georgia.

We want to hear from you. Our expert contributors have a wealth of knowledge in parenting, mental health, social media, respectful relationships, and more, and they're on call to answer your questions.

Maybe you're curious about the language you've heard from your son, brother, or partner. Perhaps you'd like to know how to have a constructive conversation about online misogyny with a young person in your life. Or maybe you want to learn more about how social media algorithms present young men with toxic content.

Submit your questions using the yellow button at the top of the page.
